_comment: The glossary, the single editable source for /glossary and its DefinedTermSet structured data. Plain language for a general reader; every definition matches what another page of the site or the docs already states, and links there. Checked against the code and the acts' official texts on 2026-09-26. Keep terms alphabetical; the page renders them in this order.

terms.definition: A digital proof of a reader's role, such as a repairer or recycler, signed by an issuer the node trusts. The reader presents it to see the restricted parts of a passport.
A data format Industry 4.0 systems use to describe products. A node can serve any published passport in this shape.
The history of everything that happened to a passport, written as it happens. Entries are only ever added, each linked to the one before, so a changed entry would show.
The passport the Batteries Regulation requires from 18 February 2027 for electric-vehicle batteries, light-transport batteries and industrial batteries over 2 kWh.
A signed copy of a passport's public page, kept outside the node so a scan still works while the node is down. It says how long it stands.
The mark on a product, usually a QR code, that carries its identifier and opens its passport when scanned.

A law the European Commission adopts under a framework regulation to fill in its detail. Under ESPR, each product group's delegated act sets whether and when its passport is required, and what it must contain.
An identity published as a small document on a company's own web domain, holding the public keys its signatures can be checked against. Anyone can look it up; no central register is involved.
A digital record that stays with a product for its whole life: what it is made of, where it came from, how to repair and recycle it. EU law is making passports compulsory one product group at a time.
A company that puts a product on the EU market or makes it available: a manufacturer, importer, distributor or similar. The passport records who is responsible.
A signature by an organisation under the EU's eIDAS Regulation. A qualified seal carries a legal presumption of integrity and origin, and only a company holding a qualified certificate can make one.
The recorded end of a product's service: recycled, destroyed, exported or lost. The passport keeps that record rather than being deleted.
The Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (EU) 2024/1781. The framework law behind passports for most product groups, whose detail arrives through delegated acts.
The European Commission's directory of registered passports, set up in July 2026. It records where each passport lives, not its content.
A web address format that carries a product's barcode number, so a phone camera can open its passport from the same code a till scans.
Moving responsibility for a passport from one company to another, recorded and signed on the passport itself.
A European standard cited in the EU's Official Journal. Following it gives a presumption that the requirements it covers are met. Six were cited for passports in July 2026.
A Commission act that sets technical or procedural detail, such as how passports are registered or the format of a disclosure.

The basis on which some readers may see more of a battery passport than the public: repairers, remanufacturers, second-life operators and recyclers for dismantling and composition work, and a battery's buyer for making it available to energy markets.
One company's own running copy of Odal Node, on infrastructure it chooses. A node serves one company and shares nothing with any other.
A group of products that share passport rules, such as batteries, textiles or toys. The group decides what a passport carries and who may read which part.
One signed file holding a passport, its signatures and its full history, which anyone can check offline without trusting us. Also called an evidence dossier.
The part of a passport anyone can read by scanning the product, with no login and no fee.
The service behind the code on a product. It turns a scan into the passport page, in the form the reader asked for.
The company in the EU that answers to authorities for a product, under market surveillance or product safety law. A passport records who it is.
The parts of a passport shown only to readers the law names, such as authorities or readers with a legitimate interest, on presentation of a credential.
The private key a company signs its passports with. It is kept on the company's own servers, encrypted, and never leaves them.
Replacing a published passport with a newer one, for example to correct a mistake. The earlier version stays readable, and a code already printed keeps working.
The identifier that ties a physical product, model or batch to its passport. European standard EN 18219 sets the schemes it may use, such as a GS1 barcode number.
A yearly report large companies publish on the unsold consumer products they discarded, why, and what happened to them. It is a company report, not a passport.
